events.title: DHS weaponizes obscure law to surveil journalists, nonprofits, and unions
events.one_liner: The Department of Homeland Security has used an obscure customs law (19 USC 1509) to demand records from journalists, nonprofits, and labor unions without judicial oversight. After a federal judge rejected search warrants against journalists Georgia Fort and Don Lemon for lacking probable cause, the DHS circumvented that ruling by obtaining Fort's six months of telephone records via administrative summons—requiring only agency approval rather than court authorization.
takeaways: DHS invoked 19 USC 1509, a customs duty provision, to bypass judicial review
Georgia Fort's six-month phone records obtained without notification or right to contest
Judge previously rejected search warrants against Fort and Lemon for insufficient probable cause
Administrative summons required only DHS official approval, not judicial authorization
Recipients instructed to keep requests confidential
